reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from a single paper shows that UHV sliding on a coarse-grained HEA leads to low friction via dynamic grain refinement and a grain-size-dependent strength model, and notes high grain-boundary energy with possible decohesion. However, the evidence does not demonstrate a ductile-to-brittle transition, cavitation, or a critical 10–50 nm grain size for embrittlement; it primarily addresses friction and softening, not toughness loss. Thus, the key premises linking refinement to brittle behavior are only partly supported.
premises: High-strain sliding in UHV dynamically refines coarse grains to ~10–50 nm
A critical nanoscale grain size triggers a shift from dislocation plasticity to grain-boundary sliding and cavitation
This mechanism-driven transition causes brittle behavior without impurity segregation
The HEA CoCrFeMnNi has a high grain-boundary energy (~0.87 J/m²) implying a propensity for decohesion even as a solid solution
The cited model predicts grain-size-dependent shear strength/friction for this HEA
